Further qualities I would ask Addleshaw Goddard to weigh include endurance under pressure, inclusive team leadership, and community-focused volunteering.

Last September I completed a climb of Mount Kilimanjaro. Long hours on the trail and turbulent weather made mental endurance essential. When teammates developed severe altitude sickness, I organised redistribution of weight from their bags across the group. Easing their loads helped them continue and meant we could finish the trek together rather than leaving people behind.

At university I served as Press Team Lead for [redacted] Model United Nations Society. I led 15 members producing content to promote the society and its annual conference, allocating roles according to individual skillsets. When some people found it hard to integrate in meetings, I arranged social events centred on communication and relationship-building. That approach improved team effectiveness and contributed to a sold-out conference.

I am also committed to volunteering in line with AG’s community ethos. I have volunteered at a youth centre supporting young people from disadvantaged backgrounds and have helped vulnerable migrant women and children in Hong Kong obtain access to legal justice. Those roles required confident handling of sensitive issues and strong service standards. Through AG’s Unlocking Young Potential strategy, I hope to contribute to work I care about deeply—promoting equality of opportunities for young people.
